original_query: SELECT * FROM (SELECT DEPTNO, NAME FROM DEPT WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP) AS t4 WHERE DEPTNO = t4.DEPTNO) ORDER BY DEPTNO) AS t3 ORDER BY DEPTNO OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY
rewritten_query: SELECT * FROM (SELECT DEPTNO, NAME FROM DEPT WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT DEPTNO FROM EMP) AS t4 WHERE DEPTNO = t4.DEPTNO) ORDER BY DEPTNO) AS t3 ORDER BY DEPTNO OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The EXISTS subquery is uncorrelated: the unqualified DEPTNO resolves to t4.DEPTNO, making the condition `DEPTNO = t4.DEPTNO` a self-comparison equivalent to `DEPTNO IS NOT NULL`. Rewritten as `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM EMP WHERE EMP.DEPTNO IS NOT NULL)`, removing the unnecessary derived table.
Removed redundant inner ORDER BY and outer wrapper subquery (SELECT * FROM ... AS t3). The outer ORDER BY with OFFSET/FETCH is sufficient and can use the dept_pkey index.
The self-comparison `DEPTNO = t4.DEPTNO` filters NULLs, simplifying to `EMP.DEPTNO IS NOT NULL`.

Recommend creating a partial index: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_emp_deptno_not_null ON EMP (DEPTNO) WHERE DEPTNO IS NOT NULL; this enables the existence check to short-circuit on first row instead of scanning 45M rows. Avoid CTEs — not needed here.
